one_month_reasoning: Window Oct 2-31, 2026. Q1 FY27 results are likely in early/mid November (Q1 FY26 was reported Nov 6, 2025), so probably outside the window; the AGM is Nov 24 (10-K). Possible in-window news: Horizon 2 delivery/acceptance by Microsoft (commissioning underway, Horizons 2-4 targeted for the December quarter), new 2027 capacity contracts (management says 'late-stage discussions'), and further GPU financings. These skew slightly positive but are offset by ATM selling and a run of cautious sell-side initiations (Redburn Neutral $40, Jones Hold). No scheduled hard catalyst, so I center a lognormal at ~$40.5 with monthly sigma ~0.29 (107% annual vol / 3.5, trimmed a bit), essentially symmetric around the current price.

fair_value.method: Blend of a capacity-driven DCF ($16/share at Oct-27: WACC 10.5%, long-run $17m revenue/MW, 68% EBITDA margin, $27.5bn FY27 capex, $32m/MW GPU refresh every 6 years, 2.5% terminal growth; weight 0.4) and 8.5x Oct-27 NTM EBITDA of ~$6.0bn less ~$27.6bn net debt incl. prepayments over 539m shares ($43; weight 0.6).

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: FY27-FY33 FCFF: revenue $2.8bn -> $8.1bn -> $14.5bn -> $21.3bn -> $25.5bn -> $28.9bn -> $31.5bn; EBITDA margin 45%/62%/68%; capex $27.5bn FY27 then $15.2bn, $14.5bn, $12.0bn, ~$11-12bn; WACC 10.5%; g 2.5%; adjusted net debt $1.6bn; 450m diluted shares; EV $7.7bn -> $13.5 now, $16 at Oct-27

inputs_detail.derivation: TIKR-reported consensus FY27 (June-27) revenue ~$2.8bn; consistent with $1bn operating ARR today ramping to >$4bn contracted ARR by Dec-26 per FY26 release.
~600MW avg revenue-generating IT capacity x $13.5m/MW; guidance of 0.3GW IT delivered 2026 and 0.8GW cumulative 2027 (FY26 release/call); slightly above $7.3-7.56bn consensus (TIKR, 24/7 Wall St).

Company targets 0.8GW IT cumulative by end-2027 and >5GW pipeline (Sweetwater, Kiowa, Bundey, Badajoz); I haircut post-2027 growth to roughly JPM's 2,065MW-by-2030 path, delayed ~2-3 years for financing/execution.

Microsoft contract = $1.94bn/200MW = $9.7m/MW; current $4bn ARR on ~300MW = $13.3m/MW; recent 3-yr contracts >$20m/MW and discussions ~$25m/MW; JPM uses $13m. Lifecycle blend assuming older GPUs reprice lower: $17m (FY29 ramps from $13.5m).

Microsoft est. project EBITDA margin 85% before corporate overhead; Q4 FY26 adj. EBITDA margin 14% on ramp costs (SG&A $128m/qtr); JPM models ~65%; 68% = 85% project less ~12-17pts corporate/power/software.
FY26 SBC $205m plus 2 x 9.1m co-CEO RSUs (10-K subsequent events) vesting over 4 years.
Midpoint of CFO guidance $25-30bn; 10-K capital commitments $13.8bn at June 30, 2026.
Microsoft: GPUs $5.8bn/200MW = $29m/MW + data center $14-16m/MW = ~$44m/MW; CFO said data center and GPU capex per MW rising ~15-20% -> ~$50m.
10-K books HPC hardware over 5 years; Q3 call notes older GPUs (H100) lasting longer than expected -> 6-yr economic life; GPU cost/MW from Microsoft/Dell figure plus inflation.
Blend of US 21%/Australia 30% statutory; 10-K shows FY26 tax benefit and valuation allowances.

Cost of equity 15.2% = 10y UST 5.24% (Treasury, 10/1/26) + beta 2.0 x ERP 5.0% (Damodaran long-run implied range 4-6%; beta 2.0 judged from 107% realized vol and 10-K volatility risk factors); pre-tax debt ~6% (GPU financing 6.0% IG / 9.0% non-IG, converts 0-1% coupon) -> 4.5% after tax; ~45% debt weight given GPU-financing-heavy funding.

methods.inputs: 8.5x x $6.0bn NTM EBITDA = $51bn EV - $27.6bn net debt incl. deferred revenue = $23.4bn / 539m shares

IREN ~10x NTM today, MARA ~10x, Nebius ~17x, Core Scientific ~19x (TIKR). Discount to today as growth slows and leverage rises; GPU-heavy capex intensity merits less than colocation peers.

inputs_detail.input: Net debt incl. deferred revenue at Oct-2027
inputs_detail.derivation: June-26 adjusted $1.6bn + FY27 FCFF deficit $26.6bn (capex $27.5bn midpoint) + one quarter of FY28 deficit ~$2.6bn + ~$0.8bn after-tax interest - ~$4bn new equity (CFO: ~$3bn equity raised in last 12 months; $3.5bn ATM capacity left under the $6bn program per 10-K).

bear.story: Horizons 2-4 or Childress air-cooled slip into 2027, the 2027 capacity (0.5GW) is contracted late or at lower prices than the >$20m/MW headline, and funding the $25-30bn FY27 capex takes more equity at low prices plus 9%-type GPU debt. Market moves to ~6x depressed EBITDA on ~$28bn+ net debt; the convert/ATM overhang keeps the stock near or below the $28.93 52-week low.

base.story: >$4bn ARR largely live by early 2027, mining shut by Dec-26, FY28 revenue ~$7.5-8.5bn in line with consensus. But capex intensity, rising net debt and ~20% more shares cap the multiple near 8-9x NTM EBITDA; the DCF says long-run GPU refresh economics leave little excess value, so the stock ends roughly flat to slightly down.

bull.story: 2027 capacity fully contracted at $20-25m/MW with 45-55% prepayments; investment-grade financing for the frontier-lab deal; 2028 pipeline (Sweetwater/Kiowa) contracted. Investors look to FY29 EBITDA >$9bn and re-rate toward 11-13x (Nebius/CORZ range), in line with JPM $65 and Street ~$76-78 targets and more.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$24 (about 17% under the 52-week low and roughly the DCF value plus a small premium), the market would be pricing a real fundamental break rather than volatility: e.g. a Microsoft tranche delay or termination that triggers the parent guarantee on the GPU financing, failure to fund the FY27 capex without heavy dilution, or GPU rental pricing collapsing so that the 2027 build earns below its cost of capital. At that level my base view (contracted ARR delivered, ~8.5x NTM EBITDA) would be wrong.

reasoning: Primary documents show IREN is in mid-pivot. FY26 revenue was $707m (AI cloud $129m). There is $1bn operating ARR, $4bn contracted for Dec-26, and $16.6bn of RPO plus lease backlog. Cash and restricted cash are $7.6bn against $7.6bn of debt (mostly low-coupon converts) and $1.8bn of prepayments. But FY27 capex guidance of $25-30bn dwarfs that, and shares rose to 394m (+53% vs 258m at June-25), with 18.2m co-CEO RSUs and ~30m in-the-money convert shares on top. A capacity-driven DCF with explicit, sourced assumptions gives only ~$16/share at Oct-27 in the base case. Microsoft-type economics (EBITDA ~28% of GPU cost per year) barely cover a 6-year GPU refresh, so value depends on newer contracts' >$20m/MW pricing holding over the lifecycle. On a market multiple (8.5x Oct-27 NTM EBITDA of ~$6bn, after ~$27.6bn net debt incl. prepayments and ~539m shares) it is worth ~$43. Blended fair value is ~$32.4, below the $40.65 price; the Street (~$76-78 mean, JPM $65) is much higher, and recent initiations (Redburn $40, Jones Hold) are closer to me. For the distribution I use a lognormal with median $35 (between fair value and spot, plus a high-beta return) and sigma 0.75. That is below the 107% realized vol because some of that was event-driven, but still wide given leverage and binary execution. Scenario check: bear $18/30%, base $38/45%, bull $80/25% gives a mean of ~$42.5, consistent with the ladder's P(>=41)=0.42. I capped P(>=$10.16) at 0.94 because of the leverage. Research was mostly primary filings; Alpha Vantage and Twelve Data estimate endpoints were unavailable (rate limit or plan), so consensus figures come from secondary articles.
